R2B-moose-drive-0004.name: 130 m S of Bridge River
R2B-moose-drive-0004.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R2B-moose-drive-0004.parkWhat: pull off on Bridge River FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: 4 wetlands within 2 km; nearest 19.3 ha, 210 m N.
Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), right here: browse.

flags.t: MU (Management Unit) 3-33, Region 3 Thompson. Near the MU line: check the MU map.

seasonRows.notes: Bag 1; spike fork bulls: antlers must accompany the species licence (page footnote)

plan: Drive: from District of Squamish, about 149 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.816, -123.18084, pull off on Bridge River FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: none. The spot is at the road.
Hunt: moose, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass the wetland and cutblock edges at dawn and dusk. Move slowly, stop often (Tip).
Use: .308 Winchester, 165 to 180 grain premium bullet, shots inside about 200 m (219 yd) (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 3-33, Region 3. Season: moose spike fork bulls Oct 15 to Nov 15 (synopsis page 34, 99%). 1 legal flag below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R2B-moose-drive-0004.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 3-33: about 260 hunter days a year for moose (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.11 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.0 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
